title: Crimes Legislation Amendment (Law Enforcement Integrity, Vulnerable Witness Protection and Other Measures) Bill 2013

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Proposed a bill strengthening laws on corruption, vulnerable witness protection and people-smuggling prosecutions, including removing wrist X-rays as a method for determining a crew member's age, and noted a review of twenty-eight disputed people-smuggling age cases led to 15 crew being released early from prison on licence.

speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Supported most measures in the Crimes Legislation Amendment (Law Enforcement Integrity, Vulnerable Witness Protection and Other Measures) Bill 2013 but flagged concerns about schedule 3's removal of wrist X-rays from age determination for people-smuggling crew, and called for Senate committee scrutiny given the AFP's 2011 clarification that the test assesses ages between 11 and 19 years.

speeches.speaker: Chris Hayes
speeches.brief: Supported the Crimes Legislation Amendment bill, describing each people-smuggling vessel as a million-dollar profit centre for its organisers, and said the parliament had just learned of another 55 people dying at sea from an asylum-seeker boat, while backing new telecommunications interception powers to disrupt organised crime.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Summed up the Crimes Legislation Amendment bill, saying removing wrist X-rays from age determination for people-smuggling crew responds to recommendations from two prior Senate inquiries and an Australian Human Rights Commission report, and said the bill extends witness protections such as video-link evidence to victims of human trafficking and slavery.

speeches.speaker: George Brandis
speeches.brief: The Coalition supported the Crimes Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 as making sensible technical changes to investigations and prosecutions of people-smuggling crew, but strongly criticised the rushed 40-hour submission period that undermined public scrutiny and Senate committee processes. Specific provisions included removing wrist X-rays for age determination due to scientific concerns and placing the burden of proof on the prosecution to establish a person was an adult at the time of an offence.
